_: English for Latin hymns whose English office (iBreviary) has no translation of them: plain line-for-line translations made for this app, a strophe per array. Keys as in match.json.
christe caelorum habitator: O Christ, kind dweller in the heavens,
life of the saints, their way, their hope and their salvation,
receive in your mercy the offering
of praise we make to you.
The choir of all the angels ever
blesses you in the heavens on high,
By the merits of the holy Virgin Mary
and of all the faithful alike,
hold back, O loving Lord, the punishment we deserve,
Grant that we may celebrate your praise here,
so that, faithful to you, we may go on with it
in heaven, singing to the Trinity
christe pastorum caput: O Christ, head and prince of shepherds,
your faithful people, glad to keep this feast,
sing to you in sacred song
the praises that are your due.
Making him your chosen minister
and joining him to your priesthood, you gave him
to stand by your people as a faithful leader
and a good provider.
He was the guide and pattern of the flock,
a light to the blind, a relief to the wretched,
a provident father to all,
made all things to all.
O Christ, who give in heaven the crown deserved
to your saints, make us follow this master
in our lives with docile hearts, and at the last
come to an end like his.
Let equal praise extol the Father most high
and you, O Saviour, loving King, for ever;
let the glory of the Holy Spirit resound
through all the world. Amen.
christe qui splendor: O Christ, who are the brightness and the day,
you lay bare the darkness of the night;
we believe you Light of light,
proclaiming light to the blessed.
We pray you, holy Lord,
guard us through this night;
let our rest be in you;
grant us quiet hours.
If our eyes are given to sleep,
let our heart keep watch for you always;
and may your right hand protect
the faithful who love you.
Look upon us, our defender,
hold back those who lie in wait;
govern your servants,
whom you have bought with your blood.
To you, O Christ, most loving King,
and to the Father be glory,
with the Spirit, the Paraclete,
for everlasting ages. Amen.
christe redemptor omnium: drive away from us all evils,
to be saved by your prayers.

doctor aeternus coleris: You are worshipped as the eternal and loving Teacher,
O Christ, who open the laws of salvation,
who alone are rightly held
to have the words of life.
We acclaim you, good Shepherd of the world,
who from heaven have ever made firm the words
of your Bride, so that through them she might
be a steady light to the world.
You yourself give shining servants,
like golden stars flashing forth,
who open to us the sure teaching
of the blessed life.
And so let them sing your praises, O Master,
who pour forth the wondrous gifts of the Spirit
through the mouths of the doctors, by which
your kindly light is mightily shown.
And may the just man whose feast we keep now plead
that you let your people walk
the pleasant ways of light, until they sing to you
hymns in the fullness of light. Amen.

iesu salvator saeculi: Jesus, saviour of the world,
come to the help of the redeemed;
and you, loving Mother of God,
ask salvation for the wretched.
May all the companies of angels,
the ranks of the patriarchs
and the merits of the prophets
beg pardon for us.
May your forerunner the Baptist
and the keeper of heaven's keys,
with the other apostles,
loose us from the bond of sin.
May the holy choir of martyrs,
the confession of priests
and the chastity of virgins
wash us from our sins.
May the prayers of monks
and all the citizens of heaven
favour the prayers of your suppliants
and ask for the reward of life.
Glory to you, O Christ,
with the Father and the Holy Spirit,
in whose wondrous light
the saints rejoice for ever. Amen.
